report: Stephen showed increased signs of restlessness and confusion tonight, evidenced by his frequent attempts to get out of bed, despite being advised to remain in bed for safety. He remains nonverbal with staff but did nod when asked if he was in pain, pointing to his lower back. His regular night-time analgesia was administered as per his care plan, but he continued to shift uncomfortably, suggesting poor pain control. We have scheduled a care plan review to reassess Stephen’s pain management.

Martha did not eat her breakfast this morning; she appeared nauseous and pushed the tray away when it was brought to her. She also reported difficulty swallowing her medication. Later, she was observed to be very fatigued and disinterested in her usual activities, such as looking through magazines. The speech therapist has been contacted to perform a swallowing assessment. Hydration is maintained through regular sips of water with the use of a cup with a spout.

John has been experiencing severe breathlessness since early afternoon. He was visibly distressed and rated his breathlessness as 7/10. Immediate administration of oxygen therapy provided little relief. He did not participate in any social activities today, preferring to remain in bed where he seemed relatively more comfortable. His respiratory rate and saturation levels are being closely monitored, and the palliative care team will evaluate his situation promptly.

Betty has struggled with significant pain in her abdomen today, rating her pain 9/10. The prescribed analgesia did not alleviate her symptoms. She did not partake in her usual grooming routines and required full assistance to perform morning hygiene tasks. Her appetite remains poor; she only took a few spoonfuls of lunch. An urgent review of her pain management protocol is ongoing, and her GP has been notified for further investigation.

Frank showed symptoms of intense agitation and was repeatedly pressing the call bell, reporting pain in his joints. He was reluctant to move from his wheelchair due to fear of falling, which has been a recurring issue. His prescribed laxatives were given since he reported no bowel movements for three days, which may be contributing to his discomfort. His family is scheduled for a care plan meeting to discuss adjustments in his palliative care regimen.

Stephen exhibited signs of breathlessness during the evening, rated the discomfort at a level of 7/10. He was using his walking aid when the breathlessness began and had to sit down immediately. After administering his prescribed bronchodilator, there was minimal improvement. Contacted the palliative care team for further review. Stephen's mobility remains compromised at the moment.

Janet complained of a sharp back pain, particularly when trying to lie flat on her bed. She rated the pain as a 9/10, and her facial expressions indicated significant discomfort. Analgesics did little to relieve the pain. Elevated her upper body with pillows which provided mild relief. Requested an urgent review of her pain management plan by the palliative care team.

Carlos felt severe nausea today, especially after eating lunch. He consumed very little of his meal and required full assistance. Given his recent history of gastrointestinal issues, antiemetics were administered, which somewhat alleviated his symptoms. A note has been made to re-evaluate his current palliative care regimen with the healthcare team.

Miranda was found to be particularly restless and showing signs of confusion this morning, unable to recognize long-time staff members. She was also observed wandering in the hallway, expressing distress when redirected to her room. Discussed the incident with the palliative care nurse, who suggested a review of her medications and potential environmental adjustments to soothe her agitation.

Henry struggled to catch his breath during his routine walks using his wheelchair. He reported feeling a tightness in his chest and his skin appeared slightly pale. Administered his prescribed emergency medications, but with limited effect. Contacted the on-call GP for immediate attention and noted to reassess his palliative care plan to address these escalating symptoms.

Stephen complained of sharp, localized pain at a 7/10 intensity in his lower back this afternoon. He received his prescribed analgesia, which only brought minimal relief. His skin remains intact and shows no signs of pressure ulcers. A note has been made for the doctor to review his pain management plan as he has no PRN medication available. Stephen remains uncomfortable and requested assistance to change positions frequently.

Eleanor was observed to be restless and wandering around her room during the night. When asked, she seemed confused and unable to orient herself to time and place. Her skin showed signs of mild redness on her lower back, likely from prolonged sitting, though no open areas were evident. Morning cares were necessary to assist her with washing, dressing, and oral hygiene due to her persistent weakness. The family has been notified of her restless behavior, and a care conference is scheduled.

Louis has been experiencing increasing breathlessness and discomfort throughout the day, particularly when lying down. His oxygen therapy is being administered as prescribed but seems to offer limited relief. He ate only a small portion of his breakfast and required encouragement to drink fluids. A visit from his granddaughter appeared to lift his spirits briefly. Continued monitoring of his respiratory status is required, and an update was given to the primary care physician.

Martha presented with visible oedema in her lower extremities and has reported a slight increase in nausea. Her appetite remains poor; she only managed a few spoonfuls of soup for lunch. She required full assistance with grooming and getting dressed this morning. Efforts to keep her hydrated are ongoing. The nurse has contacted her prescriber to discuss the potential adjustment of her diuretic medication. Despite these challenges, Martha showed interest in joining an organized group activity for a short period.

Henry's family voiced concerns about his increased agitation and reports of significant back pain this evening. Visual inspection revealed slight peeling of the skin around his lumbar region, but no pressure sores were identified. He needed encouragement during mealtime and was reminded to use adapted cutlery. PRN medication was not available for immediate pain relief, prompting a call to the physician for reassessment. Assistance with transfers and mobility has been crucial due to his ongoing discomfort. Henry was settled in bed with support pillows to ensure better comfort.

Mrs. Thompson appeared very restless throughout the day, frequently shifting in her wheelchair. Reports indicate she experienced back pain rated as 7/10 despite receiving her prescribed pain relief. The pain seemed to increase with any movement, and she needed full assistance when being transferred to bed. A message was left for her GP to revisit her pain management plan.

Mr. Leonard showed signs of increased confusion this afternoon, frequently misplacing items and mistaking the day for night. Despite this, he remained socially engaged, enjoying a visit from his daughter. He consumed only half of his lunch, declining further bites even with encouragement. Noted presence of mild oedema in lower limbs; legs elevated, but monitoring will be continued.

Ms. Rivera's skin was noted to have redness and slight peeling on her left heel, likely due to limited mobility. She expressed discomfort and rated it at 6/10. Scheduled a dressing change and initiated use of a pressure-relieving mattress. Declined an afternoon activity due to feeling overly fatigued, opting instead for time in her room browsing through a magazine.

Mr. Huang needed assistance with evening hygiene routines, and he appeared breathless after minimal exertion. Reported feeling of tightness in his chest. Offered PRN medication which brought slight relief. Increased monitoring throughout the night was implemented, and oxygen saturation levels were checked. Awaiting feedback from GP regarding his ongoing symptoms.

Ms. Allen exhibited increased agitation this evening, disoriented and attempting to wander around the corridor. Pain in her hips was rated at 5/10, although no visible injuries were noted. Observed difficulty in staying asleep, waking up multiple times feeling anxious and uncomfortable. Multidisciplinary follow-up scheduled to reassess her nighttime agitation and pain control.

Stephen described pain at a level of 7/10 in his lower back this afternoon. He received his scheduled analgesia, which offered minimal relief. The area showed no visible abnormalities, but Stephen required extensive support for repositioning due to discomfort. Increased analgesic prescription has been discussed with the GP.

Mary experienced breathlessness earlier today while sitting in her room. Oxygen therapy was started per her care plan, bringing slight improvement. Her vital signs were stable, but Mary expressed anxieties related to her breathing difficulties. The possibility of adjusting her oxygen settings has been brought to the physician's attention.

John reported feeling nausea and a sense of fullness before lunch. His antiemetic medication provided partial relief. John managed to eat a small portion of lunch with encouragement but showed obvious discomfort. His current medication regime is under review to manage these symptoms more effectively.

Margaret woke up disoriented and restless last night, expressing confusion about her surroundings. She was gently reassured and repositioned comfortably in bed. Monitoring revealed heightened agitation, and her medications for agitation required reassessment. A family meeting has been proposed to address her care adjustments.

David's pain in his left hip intensified this evening, reported as 9/10. Despite receiving breakthrough analgesia, his discomfort remained acute. David required full assistance moving from his chair to bed to mitigate pain. Urgent consultation with his healthcare provider is underway to explore stronger pain management strategies.
